3d-vcd.name: 3D-VCD
tldr: We introduce 3D-VCD, a training-free method for reducing hallucinations in embodied agents reasoning about 3D scenes. By contrasting predictions from the observed scene with deliberately distorted versions, 3D-VCD suppresses answers unsupported by the scene’s objects and geometry.

additionalSources: Results on the HEAL Probing Set

contributions: 3D-VCD as a New Inference Framework. We introduce 3D-VCD, the first training-free, inference-time contrastive decoding framework for hallucination mitigation in 3D embodied agents.

Semantic and Geometric Distortion Operators. We propose a simple and effective 3D counterfactual grounding mechanism that constructs distorted scene graphs through semantic and geometric perturbations, and uses dual-context logit fusion to suppress predictions unsupported by the underlying 3D evidence.

Strong Generalization Without Retraining. We demonstrate 3D-VCD improves grounded reasoning across embodied hallucination benchmarks, reducing over-affirmation on 3D-POPE and lowering hallucination on HEAL with minimal computational overhead.
contributionLeads: 3D-VCD as a New Inference Framework.
Semantic and Geometric Distortion Operators.
Strong Generalization Without Retraining.

VisAnom.name: VisAnomReasoner
tldr: We introduce VisAnomReasoner, a compact vision-language model that detects and localizes anomalies in time-series plots and explains its decisions. Trained with visually grounded reasoning on our curated VisAnomBench dataset, VisAnomReasoner connects unusual patterns to specific time intervals and supporting evidence.
contributions: VisAnomBench provides explanation-augmented supervision. We introduce VisAnomBench, an explanation-augmented benchmark constructed from four public time-series anomaly detection datasets. Each plot is paired with anomaly interval annotations and temporally grounded, step-by-step explanations. Reasoning traces from multiple large VLMs are selected using fine-grained rewards for anomaly localization, visual groundedness, axis awareness, and clarity. The benchmark contains 2,576 training and 740 held-out test time series.

VisAnomReasoner jointly localizes and explains anomalies. We develop a parameter-efficient vision-language model by supervised fine-tuning Qwen2.5-VL-3B and Qwen2.5-VL-7B on VisAnomBench. Structured outputs separate anomaly decisions, interval localization, and reasoning, allowing the model to explain spikes, level shifts, periodic deviations, and other anomalies using evidence in the plotted time series.

Evaluation demonstrates accurate localization and cross-benchmark transfer. VisAnomReasoner improves precision and F1 by at least 21.23 and 23.87 percentage points on VisAnomBench. On TSB-AD-U, it improves precision and F1 by 9.57 and 13.39 percentage points, respectively, demonstrating generalization beyond the training benchmark.

Ablations isolate the benefit of explanation-augmented supervision. Comparisons between pretrained models, interval-only fine-tuning, and reasoning-augmented fine-tuning show that interval supervision reduces false positives, while adding grounded reasoning traces further improves precision and recall and yields more accurate temporal boundaries.
contributionLeads: VisAnomBench provides explanation-augmented supervision.
VisAnomReasoner jointly localizes and explains anomalies.
Evaluation demonstrates accurate localization and cross-benchmark transfer.
Ablations isolate the benefit of explanation-augmented supervision.

calico.name: Calico
calico.openingCaption: Across two images, Calico segments the common object (top), shared parts (middle), and parts unique to each image (bottom). The colored masks ground each answer in the corresponding pixels.
tldr: We introduce Calico, a vision-language model that compares multiple images to identify and segment common objects and shared or unique parts. Calico learns fine-grained correspondences across images, supporting reasoning about similarities and differences with pixel-level grounding.
contributions: Novel Task. We introduce the novel task of part-focused semantic co-segmentation which aims to co-segment and label common and unique parts between objects across images for granular object comparison. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to formalize this multi-image object/part co-segmentation task.

New Multi-Image Pixel-Grounded LVLM. We propose Calico (Component-Focused Adaptive Learning for Multi-Image Co-Localization of Objects), an LVLM designed for part-focused semantic co-segmentation. Calico incorporates a novel correspondence extraction module to learn cross-image semantic correspondences and an adaptation module to enable localized co-segmentation across multiple images in a parameter-efficient manner.

New Dataset. We introduce the MixedParts dataset for part-focused semantic co-segmentation, compiled from diverse part segmentation datasets and featuring images of logically comparable objects and parts.
contributionLeads: Novel Task.
New Multi-Image Pixel-Grounded LVLM.
New Dataset.

cogniroute.name: CogniRoute
cogniroute.openingCaption: CogniRoute combines speech, gestures, and visual context to infer requests and recognize social cues such as polite refusal.
tldr: We introduce CogniRoute, a framework that teaches omni-modal models to select the evidence each social question needs. CogniRoute guides expert routing toward relevant visual cues, audio cues, and moments in a video, improving reasoning about gestures, intent, and conversational context.
contributions: CogniRoute aligns expert routing with the evidence needed for social reasoning. We introduce a schema-guided Mixture-of-Experts framework for social video question answering. Schema-Aligned Predictive Routing (SAPR) aligns modality-pooled, layer-wise routing signatures with a training-only cognitive schema that describes evidence source, reasoning demand, and temporal scope. This connects expert allocation to the visual, audio, joint, or conflicting evidence required by each question.

Route-Aware MoE Reinforcement Learning jointly optimizes answers and expert allocation. RMRL supplies rollout-level rewards for answer correctness, modality-consistent reasoning, and cognitive temporal grounding. These complementary signals update both token generation and expert routing, encouraging correct answers whose reasoning uses the relevant modality and annotated temporal evidence.

OmniSocialBench supports diagnostic social omni reasoning. We construct a resource with 118K structured training examples, grounded reasoning traces, cognitive schema labels, and temporal evidence spans. Its manually verified evaluation split covers mental state inference, pragmatic meaning, action goals, and social norms, with checks for answer validity, evidence consistency, reasoning support, and temporal grounding.

Experiments show gains in cross-modal and temporally grounded social inference. CogniRoute achieves 59.38% average accuracy on OmniSocialBench, exceeding the strongest proprietary baseline by 15.33 points and the strongest open-source omni baseline by 26.77 points. The largest gains occur on questions requiring audio-visual coordination, conflict resolution, and temporally grounded social inference.
contributionLeads: CogniRoute aligns expert routing with the evidence needed for social reasoning.
Route-Aware MoE Reinforcement Learning jointly optimizes answers and expert allocation.
OmniSocialBench supports diagnostic social omni reasoning.
Experiments show gains in cross-modal and temporally grounded social inference.

core3d.name: CoRe3D
tldr: We introduce CoRe3D, a framework that couples language-based planning with geometric reasoning over localized 3D blocks. Joint reinforcement learning aligns semantic plans with geometric construction, enabling CoRe3D to infer objects from implicit descriptions and generate shapes faithful to their intended structure.
abstract: Recent advances in large multimodal models suggest that explicit reasoning mechanisms play a critical role in improving model reliability, interpretability, and cross-modal alignment. While such reasoning-centric approaches have been proven effective in language and vision tasks, their extension to 3D remains underdeveloped. CoRe3D introduces a unified 3D understanding and generation reasoning framework that jointly operates over semantic and spatial abstractions, enabling high-level intent inferred from language to directly guide low-level 3D content formation. Central to this design is a spatially grounded reasoning representation that decomposes 3D latent space into localized regions, allowing the model to reason over geometry in a compositional and procedural manner. By tightly coupling semantic chain-of-thought inference with structured spatial reasoning, CoRe3D produces 3D outputs that exhibit strong local consistency and faithful alignment with linguistic descriptions.
contributions: CoRe3D unifies semantic planning and geometric reasoning. We introduce a collaborative reasoning framework with two complementary levels: Semantic Chain-of-Thought for high-level planning and an octant-based Geometric Chain-of-Thought that realizes the plan through a spatially grounded reasoning trajectory over 3D octant tokens.

Collaborative reasoning interprets implicit descriptive cues. The framework reasons over challenging text prompts that require inferring the correct object or interpreting an indirect description, such as identifying the Statue of Liberty from a description of a colossal copper figure holding a torch.

3D Co-GRPO aligns semantic plans with geometric construction. We propose a multi-critic optimization method with dense 3D-aware rewards to improve language alignment, geometric structure, and robustness by coordinating the two reasoning levels.

CoRe3D extends from generation to reciprocal 3D understanding. The same framework supports tasks such as 3D-to-text captioning, demonstrating bidirectional understanding and generation and its potential as a scalable foundation for general 3D intelligence.
contributionLeads: CoRe3D unifies semantic planning and geometric reasoning.
Collaborative reasoning interprets implicit descriptive cues.
3D Co-GRPO aligns semantic plans with geometric construction.
CoRe3D extends from generation to reciprocal 3D understanding.

dash.name: DaSH
dash.openingCaption: DaSH selects useful training data from a heterogeneous pool by learning which dataset groups and individual datasets improve a target model. Hierarchical selection prioritizes relevant sources under a limited exploration budget.
tldr: We introduce DaSH, a method for selecting useful datasets from diverse repositories or institutions under limited exploration budgets. By learning which groups and datasets improve a target model, DaSH finds relevant training data efficiently while avoiding less useful sources.
contributions: We formalize the task of dataset selection from a heterogeneous pool of external datasets, a setting common in real-world workflows such as public data acquisition and cross-institutional collaboration, where data is organized into discrete, variably relevant sources.

We propose DaSH, the first dataset selection method that models dataset utility through hierarchical inference over groups and datasets, enabling efficient and robust selection under limited feedback.

We benchmark DaSH against four state-of-the-art data selection methods across two public datasets, demonstrating consistent performance improvements of up to 26.2% on Digit-Five and 10.8% on DomainNet. Ablation studies show DaSH remains robust to grouping noise and scales effectively to large dataset pools, whereas existing methods frequently select irrelevant or low-utility data samples.
contributionLeads: We formalize the task of dataset selection
We propose DaSH
We benchmark DaSH

dreampartgen.name: DreamPartGen
tldr: We introduce DreamPartGen, a text-to-3D framework that generates objects as distinct, meaningful parts. DreamPartGen coordinates each part’s geometry and appearance with the relationships described in language, producing coherent assemblies that support part editing, articulated objects, and mini-scene generation.
abstract: Understanding and generating 3D objects as compositions of meaningful parts is fundamental to human perception and reasoning. However, most text-to-3D methods overlook the semantic and functional structure of parts. While recent part-aware approaches introduce decomposition, they remain largely geometry-focused, lacking semantic grounding and failing to model how parts align with textual descriptions or their inter-part relations. We propose DreamPartGen, a framework for semantically grounded, part-aware text-to-3D generation. DreamPartGen introduces Duplex Part Latents (DPLs) that jointly model each part's geometry and appearance, and Relational Semantic Latents (RSLs) that capture inter-part dependencies derived from language. A synchronized co-denoising process enforces mutual geometric and semantic consistency, enabling coherent, interpretable, and text-aligned 3D synthesis. Across multiple benchmarks, DreamPartGen delivers state-of-the-art performance in geometric fidelity and text-shape alignment.
contributions: DreamPartGen unifies geometric, visual, and relational reasoning. We introduce a language-grounded collaborative diffusion framework for coherent and interpretable part-level text-to-3D synthesis. Persistent language-derived relational semantic latents remain active throughout denoising, rather than using text only as a one-shot condition.

Duplex Part Latents and Relational Semantic Latents encode complementary information. DPLs encode modular, disentangled part geometry and appearance, while RSLs provide text-derived local refinements and global planning signals. Synchronized co-denoising through intra-part and inter-part attention maintains geometry–appearance alignment and guides consistent part assembly.

PartRel3D provides explicit supervision for inter-part relations. We curate a large-scale relational dataset with 300K canonicalized functional and spatial triplets across 175 object categories. These annotations connect part geometry, appearance, and language through relations such as support, attach, hinge, above, touching, and aligned-with.

Experiments demonstrate coherent and controllable part-aware generation. DreamPartGen achieves state-of-the-art performance across the reported benchmarks, with gains in geometric fidelity, text–shape alignment, and controllable part-level synthesis.
contributionLeads: DreamPartGen unifies geometric, visual, and relational reasoning.
Duplex Part Latents and Relational Semantic Latents encode complementary information.
PartRel3D provides explicit supervision for inter-part relations.
Experiments demonstrate coherent and controllable part-aware generation.

ec-vlm.name: EC-VLM
ec-vlm.openingCaption: Left: a speaker describes a target image with learned EC tokens, and a listener selects that image among distractors. Center: image–message pairs pretrain a vision-language model. Right: visual grounding transfers to entailment, captioning, referring expressions, and question answering.
tldr: We introduce EC-VLM, a framework that uses communication between artificial agents to pretrain vision-language models. Messages learned in an image-based speaker–listener game provide visual supervision that transfers to tasks such as captioning, question answering, and referring-expression understanding.

quantitative.source: Quantitative Results on the Visual Entailment Task

contributions: Novel Pretraining Framework. We introduce a vision-language pretraining framework that employs Emergent Communication (EC) between agents to generate supervision signals for pretraining. We demonstrate that EC pretraining transfers effectively to diverse downstream multimodal tasks.

New Understanding of EC Structure. We empirically show that EC tokens encode structured and compositional semantics that generalize across tasks and modalities, positioning EC as a scalable, annotation-free alternative to natural language supervision in multimodal learning.

Theoretical and Empirical Insights. We provide insights into the structure and transferability of emergent language for vision-language pretraining and outline future research opportunities at the intersection of EC, multimodal representation learning, and human-machine communication.
contributionLeads: Novel Pretraining Framework.
New Understanding of EC Structure.
Theoretical and Empirical Insights.

ece.name: Embodied Confidence Elicitation
tldr: We study how embodied agents assess uncertainty in what they see and the actions they plan to take. Our framework elicits confidence through structured reasoning and alternative interpretations, evaluating how well elicited confidence predicts success and failure in Minecraft tasks.
contributions: We investigate open-world embodied confidence elicitation. We study language- and vision-language-powered agents in settings where uncertainty arises from perception and decision making, while the agents lack direct access to their internal reasoning processes.

Elicitation and execution policies address distinct forms of uncertainty. We introduce Elicitation Policies for inductive, deductive, and abductive uncertainty, together with Execution Policies for scenario reinterpretation, action sampling, and hypothetical reasoning. These policies let agents express and refine confidence through structured reasoning and interaction with the environment.

Minecraft experiments evaluate calibration and failure prediction. Structured reasoning approaches, including Chain-of-Thought, improve confidence calibration. The evaluation also identifies persistent difficulty distinguishing uncertainty under abductive settings, highlighting the need for more capable embodied confidence elicitation methods.
contributionLeads: We investigate open-world embodied confidence elicitation.
Elicitation and execution policies address distinct forms of uncertainty.
Minecraft experiments evaluate calibration and failure prediction.

editvid.name: EditVid
tldr: We introduce EditVid, a training-free framework for diverse video editing, supporting various instruction-guided and reference-guided edits in one framework, including style transfer, attribute modification, object insertion, part-level editing, and subject replacement.
contributions: EditVid unifies instruction-guided and reference-guided video editing without training. The framework extends frozen MM-DiT-based image editors to temporally consistent video editing, supporting style transfer, attribute modification, object insertion, part-level editing, and subject replacement within the same pipeline.

Sparse causal memory preserves local temporal coherence. Adjacent-frame spatio-temporal attention shares information across nearby frames, while correspondence-based post-attention token injection preserves long-range appearance and identity. Confidence- and cycle-consistent correspondences match each frame to an anchor before matched visual representations are injected after attention.

Soft latent blending maintains edit locality. Timestep-dependent preservation weights derived from source–edit trajectory discrepancies retain source content where needed while allowing the requested modification elsewhere in the video.

Benchmarks and a user study assess quality across editing paradigms. EditVid achieves 78.16 FiVE-Acc on FiVE, compared with 58.95 for the strongest evaluated training-free baseline, and obtains competitive IVEBench results. A user study reports 51.8% overall preference for EditVid over seven competing methods.

method.source: A local–global decomposition for temporal control

contributionLeads: EditVid unifies instruction-guided and reference-guided video editing without training.
Sparse causal memory preserves local temporal coherence.

egoforge.name: EgoForge
tldr: We introduce EgoForge, a framework for generating goal-directed first-person video from an image and an instruction, with an optional external view providing additional context. Reward-guided refinement aligns the video with the intended goal while preserving scene consistency and coherent motion.
contributions: EgoForge generates goal-directed first-person rollouts from minimal static inputs. We introduce an egocentric world simulator conditioned on a single egocentric image, a high-level instruction, and an optional auxiliary exocentric view. It models scene evolution and hand–object interactions without requiring camera trajectories, pose signals, or synchronized multi-view streams at inference time.

Geometry weak supervision improves spatial consistency. Intermediate diffusion-transformer representations are aligned with geometry features from a pretrained VGGT encoder. Angular alignment matches feature directions, while scale alignment prevents scale collapse and encourages spatially stable video rollouts.

GRAFT refines complete trajectories using complementary rewards. We propose trajectory-level reward-guided refinement for goal completion, scene consistency, temporal causality, and perceptual fidelity. Evaluating these signals over entire trajectories encourages the intended outcome while reducing scene drift and inconsistent motion.

Experiments test both benchmark performance and real-world use. EgoForge shows consistent improvements in semantic alignment, geometric stability, and motion fidelity over strong baselines and maintains robust performance in real-world smart-glasses experiments.

additionalSources: Qualitative Results: With vs. Without Exocentric Input

contributionLeads: EgoForge generates goal-directed first-person rollouts from minimal static inputs.
Geometry weak supervision improves spatial consistency.
GRAFT refines complete trajectories using complementary rewards.

elsa3D.name: ELSA3D
tldr: We introduce ELSA3D, a unified 3D model built around elastic semantic anchoring: sparse Anchor Tokens link selected language tokens to geometric evidence at the relevant scale. One router jointly controls anchor selection, geometric scale, block execution, and MLP width, improving language–geometry grounding while roughly halving FLOPs and inference latency compared with the non-elastic variant.
abstract: ELSA3D is a unified 3D foundation model that structures language and geometric reasoning along matched abstraction scales. Scale-aware octree tokenization retains coarse structural cues and fine geometric detail. Sparse Anchor Tokens provide an explicit cross-modal interface: selected semantic tokens retrieve geometric evidence at a routed scale and fuse it back into the unified representation. An elastic router jointly controls block execution, MLP width, anchor selection, and geometric-scale assignment. Evaluations cover image-to-3D generation, text-to-3D generation, and object captioning, with ablations examining grounding and computational efficiency.
contributions: Elastic semantic anchoring structures language and geometric reasoning jointly. ELSA3D makes text–3D interaction explicit across matched abstraction scales, rather than collapsing coarse structural cues and fine geometric detail into an undifferentiated sequence. Scale-aware octree tokenization supplies structural bits, scale-specific content codes, positional embeddings, and fixed scale tags for multiscale geometry.

Anchor Tokens provide a sparse, dynamic cross-modal interface. Each anchor selects a semantic token, routes it to the most relevant 3D scale, retrieves scale-specific geometric evidence, and writes the fused language–geometry signal back into the unified sequence, keeping interaction sparse yet precise.

An elastic router jointly controls computation and grounding. One routing scheme controls block execution, MLP width, anchor selection, and geometric-scale assignment. The elastic router concentrates cross-modal capacity where semantic–geometric alignment is needed, adapting both computation and grounding to the input.

ELSA3D improves unified 3D performance while reducing computation. The model achieves state-of-the-art results on image-to-3D generation, text-to-3D generation, and 3D captioning, outperforming the strongest unified baseline on every reported metric while roughly halving FLOPs and inference latency relative to a non-elastic variant of the same model.
contributionLeads: Elastic semantic anchoring structures language and geometric reasoning jointly.
Anchor Tokens provide a sparse, dynamic cross-modal interface.

graphvid.name: GraphVid
contributions: Interactive graph-based control. GraphVid enables multi-object image-to-video control through directed interaction scene graphs constructed from a single image, replacing dense trajectory authoring with intuitive object-level interaction edits.

Edge-Aware Graph Reasoning. A GINEConv-based graph module injects directed edge semantics into message passing so that node representations capture both object identity and interaction-driven dynamics.

Parameter-efficient graph-to-video adaptation. A lightweight graph-to-token adapter and LoRA modules condition a frozen LTX-Video 2B backbone and frozen VAE while preserving pretrained generative priors.

GraphVid-Bench and efficient performance. We curate approximately 27K interaction-centric clips with structured graphs. GraphVid uses 0.6B trainable parameters and achieves the fastest inference among the compared methods at 200 seconds.
contributionLeads: Interactive graph-based control.
Edge-Aware Graph Reasoning.
Parameter-efficient graph-to-video adaptation.
GraphVid-Bench and efficient performance.
tldr: We introduce GraphVid, a framework for controlling image-to-video generation through object interactions. Users edit a graph to specify how objects push, pull, lift, or move relative to one another, guiding coherent multi-object motion.

hallusegbench.name: RobustSeg
tldr: We introduce RobustSeg, a segmentation vision-language model trained on factual and counterfactual image pairs to ground masks in visual evidence and abstain when the queried object is absent. Our Counterfactual Segmentation Reasoning task and HalluSegBench benchmark test this distinction and measure the severity of hallucinated masks. Counterfactual fine-tuning reduces hallucinations by 30% while preserving segmentation fidelity.

paragraphs: RobustSeg is a segmentation vision-language model trained with Counterfactual Finetuning (CFT). Training pairs factual images with controlled visual counterfactuals so the model learns to segment a referenced object when visual evidence supports it and abstain when the object is absent. This counterfactual supervision helps distinguish observed evidence from contextual priors while preserving segmentation fidelity.

dataset.name: HalluSegBench
paragraphs: HalluSegBench introduces controlled visual counterfactuals for diagnosing pixel-grounding hallucinations in referring and reasoning expression segmentation. The Counterfactual Segmentation Reasoning task requires segmentation in the factual image and abstention in its counterfactual counterpart. Complementary evaluation metrics measure hallucination severity and separate vision-driven from language-driven failure modes.

contributions: New Task. To assess segmentation fidelity, we introduce the novel task of Counterfactual Segmentation Reasoning (CSR) which assesses whether segmentation models correctly adapt to counterfactual visual changes. Our experiments show that vision-driven hallucinations are far more severe than label-driven ones, highlighting critical gaps in current grounding capabilities.

New Benchmark. We curate HalluSegBench the first benchmark for pixel-grounding hallucination via counterfactual visual reasoning, and propose novel evaluation metrics that quantify hallucination along complementary dimensions.

New Model. We present RobustSeg a segmentation VLM, trained with Counterfactual Finetuning (CFT), with abstention-aware grounding capabilities. RobustSeg learns to distinguish visual evidence from contextual priors, yielding large and consistent reductions in hallucination while preserving segmentation fidelity.
contributionLeads: New Task.
New Benchmark.
New Model.

latte-flow.name: LaTtE-Flow
tldr: We introduce LaTtE-Flow, which adds image generation to a frozen vision-language model through Layerwise Timestep Experts. Each transformer layer group handles a distinct flow-matching timestep range, so only that group runs at each sampling step. Timestep-Conditioned Residual Attention reuses and refines attention across layers, delivering competitive generation quality with about six times faster inference while preserving multimodal understanding.
contributions: Layerwise Timestep Experts make unified flow-based generation more efficient. We introduce LaTtE-Flow, which inherits multimodal understanding from a frozen pretrained VLM and adds a trainable generation pathway. Transformer layers are divided into non-overlapping groups, each responsible for a distinct flow-matching timestep interval, so only the current group runs at each sampling step instead of the full stack.

Timestep-Conditioned Residual Attention reuses attention across layers. A lightweight, head-wise gate controls how much image self-attention each layer reuses from the previous layer as a function of the current timestep. Gradually refining attention speeds up training convergence and improves generation quality without additional inference cost.

Experiments demonstrate faster generation while preserving understanding. By retaining the frozen VLM backbone, LaTtE-Flow maintains strong multimodal understanding and competitive image generation quality while reaching approximately six times faster inference than recent unified multimodal models.
contributionLeads: Layerwise Timestep Experts make unified flow-based generation more efficient.
Timestep-Conditioned Residual Attention reuses attention across layers.
Experiments demonstrate faster generation while preserving understanding.

mmplanner.name: MMPlanner
tldr: We introduce MMPlanner, a framework for generating step-by-step plans with aligned text and images without task-specific training. MMPlanner reasons about how objects change throughout a procedure, keeping instructions, visual depictions, and object states consistent across the plan.
contributions: We introduce MMPlanner, a zero-shot MPP method that generates coherent multimodal plans with accurate explicit and implicit object state changes in visual plan sequences.

MMPlanner incorporates background context from previous textual steps through a novel Chain-of-Thought (CoT) with Object State Reasoning (OSR-CoT) prompting method, ensuring precise visual representations of object states across steps. OSR-CoT reduces inference time by ~46.25% compared to SoTA MPP baselines.

We propose a comprehensive evaluation framework with two metrics, T-PlanScore and CA-Score, and an evaluation task, VS-Ordering, to collectively assess the planning accuracy, cross-modal alignment, temporal coherence, and visual informativeness of the generated plans.

MMPlanner incorporates background context

mtsbench.name: mTSBench
tldr: We introduce mTSBench, a benchmark for comparing multivariate time-series anomaly detectors and selecting models when anomaly labels are unavailable. mTSBench’s unified evaluation across diverse datasets shows how detector performance changes across domains and where current model-selection methods fall short.
abstract: mTSBench is a benchmark for multivariate time-series anomaly detection and model selection. It brings together 344 labeled time series from 19 datasets across 12 application domains, and evaluates 24 statistical, deep-learning, and language-model-based detectors under a unified protocol. The benchmark also evaluates unsupervised selection methods using consistent point-based and ranking-based metrics. Results show that no single detector performs consistently well across datasets and that current model selectors remain far below oracle performance, motivating adaptive, data-aware selection strategies.

paragraphs: mTSBench evaluates anomaly detectors and unsupervised model selectors under a unified protocol. Detector comparisons cover point-based and range-aware detection metrics, runtime, and performance across datasets. Model-selection evaluations compare the selected detector with trivial and near-optimal baselines, and use ranking metrics to assess recommendations. The evaluated selectors are described below.

contributions: We introduce mTSBench, the largest and most comprehensive MTS-AD and model selection benchmark to date, featuring 344 multivariate time series from 19 datasets across 12 application domains. mTSBench systematically evaluates 24 anomaly detectors, including the only LLM-based methods for MTS-AD, reflecting their performance in multivariate settings with real-world temporal dependencies and cross-signal interactions.

Our empirical analysis reveals that, among the evaluated methods, no single anomaly detection method performs consistently well across datasets in mTSBench, underscoring the need for adaptive selection strategies. To this end, mTSBench is the first to integrate unsupervised model selection methods and benchmark their effectiveness across diverse time series contexts and under consistent settings.

To drive reproducible comparisons, mTSBench introduces a unified evaluation suite with point-based and ranking-based metrics for anomaly detection and model selection. Using this standardized setup, we observe substantial gaps between the evaluated unsupervised model selection methods and both optimal and trivial baselines. These results highlight limitations of current unsupervised selection strategies and underscore the need for more adaptive model selection mechanisms.

palm.name: PALM
tldr: We introduce PALM, a vision-language-action (VLA) model for long-horizon robotic manipulation that anticipates future interactions and tracks subtask progress. By combining visual cues about objects, contact, and motion with progress-aware action generation, PALM helps robots carry out coherent multi-step tasks.
contributions: Structured affordance foresight anticipates future interaction needs. PALM predicts factorized affordances for object relevance, contact geometry, spatial placement, and motion dynamics. These global, local, spatial, and dynamic cues help the policy reason about which object matters, where to interact, where to place or move it, and how the next interaction should unfold.

A progress-aware diffusion policy coordinates long-horizon subtasks. The policy conditions on the predicted affordances and jointly estimates actions and continuous within-subtask progress. These estimates guide continuation, transition, and termination decisions, reducing repeated or skipped actions during multi-step manipulation.

Simulation and real-world evaluations demonstrate long-horizon robustness. PALM reaches 91.8% success on LIBERO-LONG, improves average length on CALVIN ABCD by 12.5%, and achieves a twofold improvement over real-world baselines across three generalization settings: object relocation, unseen lighting, and visual distractors.
contributionLeads: Structured affordance foresight anticipates future interaction needs.
A progress-aware diffusion policy coordinates long-horizon subtasks.

part2gs.name: Part²GS
tldr: We introduce Part²GS, which jointly discovers articulated parts and learns their motion from multi-view images at two object states. Each 3D Gaussian carries a learnable part identity in a motion-aware canonical representation. Contact, velocity, and vector-field constraints keep articulation coherent, while a field of repel points prevents collisions between parts.
contributions: A part-aware Gaussian representation models articulated digital twins. We introduce Part²GS, a framework for multi-part objects with high-fidelity geometry and physically consistent articulation. Articulated components carry learnable attributes that enable structured, disentangled transformations while preserving the reconstructed geometry.

A motion-aware canonical representation enforces physically consistent motion. Contact enforcement, velocity consistency, and vector-field alignment constrain articulation, encouraging components to move coherently while maintaining their spatial relationships.
A field of repel points prevents collisions between parts. Repulsion discourages inter-part collisions and stabilizes articulation paths, improving motion coherence over the evaluated baselines.

Synthetic and real-world evaluations assess geometry and articulation. Part²GS consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, with improvements of up to tenfold in Chamfer Distance for movable parts.
contributionLeads: A part-aware Gaussian representation models articulated digital twins.
A motion-aware canonical representation enforces physically consistent motion.
A field of repel points prevents collisions between parts.
Synthetic and real-world evaluations assess geometry and articulation.

phantom.name: Phantom
tldr: We introduce PHANTOM, a physics-infused video generation framework that jointly models visual content and latent physical dynamics, producing videos that are both visually realistic and physically consistent.
contributions: We propose Phantom, a physics-infused video generation framework that jointly models visual content and latent physical dynamics through two coupled visual and physical reasoning branches.

We validate the effectiveness of Phantom in producing video sequences that are both perceptually realistic and physically coherent through extensive experiments on standard video generation and physics-aware benchmarks.
contributionLeads: We propose Phantom, a physics-infused video generation framework
We validate the effectiveness of Phantom

prima.name: PRIMA
tldr: We introduce PRIMA, a multi-image vision-language model that couples cross-image reasoning with pixel-grounded explanations. Its SQuARE module uses learnable relational queries to gather shared context across images, then injects that context into compact visual tokens before language fusion. PRIMA generates answers and segmentation masks together, trained and evaluated on M⁴Seg’s approximately 744K multi-image question-answer pairs with object and part masks.

dataset.name: M⁴Seg
paragraphs: M⁴Seg is a multi-image pixel-grounded reasoning segmentation benchmark containing approximately 744K question-answer pairs. Each example combines an image set with object and part segmentation annotations, enabling training and evaluation of reasoning grounded in pixel-level evidence across images. The benchmark covers functional, spatial, numerical, and open-ended reasoning.

contributions: Novel Task. We propose the novel task of multi-image pixel-grounded reasoning segmentation which requires fine-grained comparison and contextual understanding across multiple images at pixel level and natural language reasoning.

New Benchmark. We curate M4Seg a new challenging benchmark with ~744K multi-image QA pairs, annotated with multiple object and part segmentation masks to train and evaluate multi-image pixel-grounding models.

New Multi-Image Pixel-Grounded LVLM. We propose PRIMA an LVLM designed to perform instruction-guided cross-image alignment of relevant visual features via a novel SQuARE module, enabling reasoning with contextually grounded segmentation masks across multiple images. Experiments demonstrate PRIMA's impressive performance compared to strong baselines across segmentation (+↑8.11% mIoU and +↑7.83% Recall) and text-based metrics (+↑6.45% Semantic Similarity and +↑11.25% S-IoU).
contributionLeads: Novel Task.
New Benchmark.
New Multi-Image Pixel-Grounded LVLM.

opening.alt: PRIMA compares multiple images and grounds reasoning in segmentation masks.
opening.caption: PRIMA answers questions across images and segments the objects or parts that support each answer.

pyratok.name: PyraTok
tldr: We introduce PyraTok, a video tokenizer whose Language-aligned Pyramidal Quantization (LaPQ) discretizes features at multiple encoder depths into a shared binary codebook of approximately 48K tokens. Text guidance aligns each pyramid level locally, while an autoregressive objective aligns the token hierarchy globally. This dual alignment preserves semantic consistency across scales and time, supporting high-resolution reconstruction, generation, and zero-shot video understanding.

paragraphs: PyraTok builds on a pretrained video VAE and applies Language-aligned Pyramidal Quantization (LaPQ) at multiple encoder depths. A shared large binary codebook discretizes the resulting hierarchy into compact, semantically structured video tokens. Text-guided quantization provides local alignment at each scale, while an autoregressive objective over the token hierarchy enforces global sequence coherence. A hierarchical semantic codebook loss links the shared codebook to text embeddings and regularizes consistency across pyramid levels.

image.alt: PyraTok architecture with multi-scale Language-aligned Pyramidal Quantization, text conditioning, and autoregressive semantic alignment

contributions: Multi-scale semantically aligned VAE. We introduce PyraTok, a multi-scale semantically aligned Video VAE that couples spatiotemporal quantization with dual semantic alignment, enabling coarse-to-fine understanding and efficient video generation.

LaPQ quantization. PyraTok leverages LaPQ, a novel language-aligned pyramidal quantization framework, designed to hierarchically encode multi-scale video representations through lateral encoder connections at each stage. Our design enables efficient use of a large ∼48K token vocabulary, with up to 95% codebook utilization.

Dual semantic alignment. We propose a dual semantic alignment strategy that injects text-conditioned priors at every LaPQ level (local alignment) and refines them with an autoregressive objective over the sequence of quantized tokens (global alignment). This jointly enforces token-level grounding and sequence-level coherence, preventing semantic drift across scales and time.

Hierarchical semantic codebook loss. We further introduce a hierarchical semantic codebook loss that ties a shared binary codebook to text embeddings and preserves semantic consistency across pyramid levels through stage-wise KL regularization.
contributionLeads: Multi-scale semantically aligned VAE.
LaPQ quantization.
Dual semantic alignment.
Hierarchical semantic codebook loss.

rewardflow.name: RewardFlow
tldr: We introduce RewardFlow, a training-free framework for image generation and editing that guides pretrained models with complementary rewards. RewardFlow adapts to each instruction, balancing prompt alignment, visual quality, and localized changes without inversion or model fine-tuning.

paragraphs: RewardFlow fuses complementary differentiable reward gradients into a multi-reward Langevin sampling update. A prompt-aware policy parses the instruction and adapts reward weights and step sizes throughout sampling. Fine-grained guidance includes a differentiable VQA reward and a SAM2 text-guided object reward to improve attribute correctness and localize edits. A clean-latent KL regularizer tethers sampling to the originating latent, controlling drift while the fused guidance steers generation or editing.

image.alt: Source images paired with attention-localization maps for changing juice type, changing shoe color, creating a Ghibli-style portrait, and adding glasses.
image.caption: Source images and attention-localization maps for attribute changes, portrait stylization, and adding glasses.

contributions: RewardFlow. We introduce a multi-reward-guided Langevin framework that combines semantic, perceptual, regional, object-level, and human-preference signals to enable controllable, inversion-free editing and generation.

Prompt-aware adaptive policy. Our lightweight policy parses semantic primitives from the instruction, infers edit intent, and dynamically adjusts reward weights and step sizes to balance coarse-to-fine optimization.
Fine-grained rewards. We design a differentiable VQA reward for attribute-level correctness and a SAM-guided localization reward that penalizes edits leaking outside the region of interest.

Theoretical grounding. We prove the update corresponds to a valid discretization of a Langevin SDE targeting a prompt-tilted density, giving a sound foundation for stable convergence during reward-guided sampling.
contributionLeads: RewardFlow.
Prompt-aware adaptive policy.
Fine-grained rewards.
Theoretical grounding.

silsa.name: SILSA
tldr: We introduce SILSA, a framework for generating high-resolution 3D shapes from a single image using compact slice-based representations. SILSA coordinates overlapping slices across three axes and preserves thin structures, holes, and connectivity, producing detailed shapes with substantially fewer tokens.
contributions: Sliding-window slice latents provide a compact representation of 3D shapes. We introduce SILSA, a topology-aware generation framework that replaces expensive local voxel tokens with a fixed set of overlapping depth-window slices along the three canonical axes. The representation preserves cross-sectional continuity and supports single-stage rectified-flow generation.

SliceVAE and a Volumetric Anchor Lattice coordinate reconstruction. A Slice VAE encodes oriented surface samples into multi-axis slice latents and reconstructs geometry with a sparse volumetric decoder. A shared 3D anchor workspace coordinates the directional slice streams.

Slice-level topology supervision preserves structural correctness. Persistence-diagram matching and Betti-transition alignment across neighboring slices encourage correct cross-sectional topology, preserving thin structures, repeated components, and long-range connectivity.

Experiments measure structural fidelity and generation cost. SILSA improves PSNR by 8.7%, coverage by 5.96 absolute points, and Betti error by 9.2% over the strongest baseline. It uses 70.0% fewer tokens than the next-most compact baseline and over 98% fewer than sparse or hierarchical tokenizers, reducing training memory by 40.4% and inference time by 58.5%.
contributionLeads: Sliding-window slice latents provide a compact representation of 3D shapes.

spatialreasoner.name: SpatialReasoner-R1
tldr: We introduce SpatialReasoner-R1, a model for answering fine-grained spatial questions with interpretable, step-by-step reasoning. SpatialReasoner-R1 learns to connect descriptions and logical deductions to visible spatial evidence, helping models reason about object locations, relationships, and layouts.
contributions: SpatialReasoner-R1. We introduce SpatialReasoner-R1, a VLM designed for fine-grained LongCoT spatial reasoning that effectively generates interpretable, step-by-step explanations directly from 2D images. SpatialReasoner-R1 establishes a new SoTA in spatial understanding tasks, while maintaining robust performance on general vision-language benchmarks.

Fine-grained Direct Preference Optimization. To enhance training stability and precision, we propose a new fine-grained Direct Preference Optimization fDPO method that employs segment-specific learning updates tailored explicitly for descriptive grounding and logical reasoning.

Multi-Model Monte Carlo Tree Search. To address the scarcity of high-quality spatial reasoning data, we introduce a data generation pipeline that combines Multi-Model Monte Carlo Tree Search (M3CTS) with fine-grained spatial rewards, enabling the creation of diverse, logically consistent LongCoT trajectories for fine-grained preference training.
contributionLeads: SpatialReasoner-R1.
Fine-grained Direct Preference Optimization.

unidflow.name: UniDFlow
tldr: We introduce UniDFlow, a discrete flow-matching model that unifies image understanding, generation, and reasoning-guided editing. Separate text and image LoRA adapters preserve specialized capabilities, while a lightweight Mixture-of-LoRA router composes them during diffusion. Multimodal Reference-based DPO (mRef-DPO) uses a visual reference and structured reflection traces to align edits with instructions, geometry, and physical transformations.
contributions: UniDFlow unifies multimodal understanding, generation, and editing. We introduce a discrete flow-matching framework that bridges high-level visual reasoning and high-fidelity image synthesis within a unified model.

Task-specific adapters prevent interference between understanding and generation. Separate text and image LoRA adapters are trained while keeping the backbone frozen; KL regularization helps preserve linguistic ability. A lightweight Mixture-of-LoRA (MoRA) router dynamically composes the adapters during diffusion, combining their specialized capabilities.

Multimodal reference-based preference alignment improves faithful editing. mRef-DPO compares outcomes under identical conditioning against a frozen reference policy and a visual reference image. Structured reflection traces help the model reason through geometric, physical, and temporal transformations before generating the edited image.

Evaluation demonstrates broad performance and zero-shot generalization. UniDFlow achieves state-of-the-art performance across eight benchmarks and generalizes to inpainting, in-context image generation, reference-based editing, and compositional generation without explicit task-specific training for those tasks.
contributionLeads: UniDFlow unifies multimodal understanding, generation, and editing.

vtam.name: VTAM
tldr: We introduce VTAM, a video–tactile–action model for contact-rich robotic manipulation. By combining visual observations with touch, VTAM predicts actions and object dynamics while capturing contact and deformation, providing physically grounded guidance for tasks where vision alone is insufficient.
contributions: VTAM grounds contact-rich manipulation in visual and tactile signals. We introduce a Video-Tactile Action Model that augments a pretrained video transformer with tactile perception. This complements visual observations with force and contact information that vision alone cannot reliably encode.

Modality transfer fine-tuning adds tactile perception efficiently. The model learns cross-modal representations without tactile–language paired data or independent tactile pretraining. Its first stage learns joint visuo-tactile predictive dynamics through multi-view diffusion over two RGB views and one GelSight stream.

Tactile regularization and joint action–state–force prediction preserve sensitivity. A regularization loss balances cross-modal attention to prevent visual latents from dominating. In the control stage, conditional diffusion jointly predicts actions, states, and a deformation-derived virtual force proxy, preserving tactile sensitivity during multimodal optimization.

Real-world experiments demonstrate improved contact-rich control. VTAM achieves 90% average success across chip pick-and-place, cucumber peeling, and whiteboard wiping, with task success rates of 90%, 85%, and 95%, respectively. On potato chip pick-and-place, it exceeds the vision-only pi 0.5 baseline by 80 percentage points.
contributionLeads: VTAM grounds contact-rich manipulation in visual and tactile signals.
